newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso signs telecom bill into law.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso signs telecom bill into law.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso signed into law Wednesday a bill that allows the government to privatize federal telecommunications holding Telebras.
The General Telecommunications Law also creates a new regulator for the sector, the National Telecommunications Agency (ANATEL), and lays down rules for private operators.

"The Brazilian state is reforming itself with the support of Congress and thanks to the courage of Communications Minister (Sergio Motta)...in breaking certain technocratic, bureaucratic and self-serving cliques," Cardoso said.

The Brazilian government hopes to begin privatizing Telebras next year, starting with Sao Paulo state subsidiary Telesp and long-distance carrier Embratel. Analysts say Telesp may be privatized for as much as $25 billion.
In his speech Wednesday, Cardoso stressed the improvements the sell-off of the telecommunications industry would bring Brazil as a whole.

He said Brazil's ailing telecommunications system would be expanded to include remote regions and urban shanty-towns which are poorly served by the existing network. Brazilian research and development into telecommunications technology would also benefit from the law, the president said.
